| 2026-08-22 | W4 (part 3) · F2's `/login` hot-apply fix via a new `CatalogRefreshFactory` seam — **F2 closed (both its sub-requirements); F5, F10, F11, F9 still open, W4 as a whole stays open** | Third implementation slice of W4, directly on top of part 2 (PR #202, merged `12ea6bf`), closing the concrete gap part 1's own entry had already named: `internal/tui/login.go`'s `finishLogin` returned to `ModeChat` after a successful `/login` but never triggered a catalog refresh or engine rebuild, leaving a freshly-authenticated provider unusable until a separate `--refresh`/restart. **Root-caused before writing code, per this project's own "no quick fixes" rule**: a successful login writes the new credential to disk (`config.SaveProviderConnection`/`SaveCredential`, `internal/app/loginfactory.go`'s `loginWaiter.Wait`), but the running session's in-memory `*config.Config` — `Root.cfg`, and the exact pointer `NewEngineFactory`/`NewLoginFactory`'s own closures captured at boot — is a snapshot taken once by `config.Load` in `app.Run` and never sees that write. A naive fix (re-running `catalog.Build`/`RefreshCatalog` against the same stale `cfg` pointer) would have reproduced the pre-login catalog exactly, silently defeating the whole point of F2; the real fix has to re-run `config.Load` from disk, not just re-run discovery. Also confirmed, via targeted greps across `internal/tui/picker.go`, `internal/catalog/model.go`, `internal/catalog/merge.go`, that F2's other named sub-requirement ("omniroute in the selection list") needed **no code change at all** — no special-case exclusion of the omniroute provider id exists anywhere in the picker/catalog resolution flow; it already flows through the same generic machinery as any other provider. **Design decided before writing code.** A new `CatalogRefreshFactory func(ctx context.Context) (*catalog.Catalog, *config.Config)` seam (`internal/tui/catalogrefresh.go`) mirrors the existing nil-safe `EngineFactory`/`LoginFactory` pattern exactly: nil is a supported value ("nothing wired"), and `finishLogin` nil-checks before using it. It deliberately returns a *second*, independent `*config.Config` value rather than mutating the shared pointer in place from inside the `tea.Cmd`'s own goroutine — that goroutine runs concurrently with Update/View's single goroutine, which may be reading `m.cfg` (e.g. `/config`, `/debug`) at the exact same moment, so mutating shared state there would be a real data race, not a theoretical one. The fresh value instead travels back on the pre-existing `CatalogRefreshedMsg` (extended with a new `Cfg *config.Config` field, nil for the §4.4/§11 background refresh, set for this new trigger) and is applied by `applyCatalogRefreshed`, which runs on Update's own goroutine. **The one open design question part 1's entry had flagged as unresolved — whether `engineFor`'s closure (built once at boot over the old `cfg` pointer by `NewEngineFactory(cfg, ...)`) would need rebuilding after a hot config swap — resolved cleanly without any rebuild**: `applyCatalogRefreshed` copies the fresh config's fields into the exact struct `m.cfg` already points at (`*m.cfg = *msg.Cfg`, not `m.cfg = msg.Cfg`), so `engineFor`'s existing closure — which holds that same pointer value, not a way to observe `Root.cfg`'s field being reassigned — sees the reload automatically, for free. `config.Config` is a plain struct with no internal pointers/mutexes, confirmed safe for this shallow in-place copy. **What landed.** `internal/tui/catalogrefresh.go` (new): `CatalogRefreshFactory` plus `refreshCatalogCmd`, wrapping a factory call as a `tea.Cmd` and reusing `CatalogRefreshedMsg` rather than a bespoke message type, so this new trigger and the pre-existing background refresh land on the exact same `applyCatalogRefreshed` handler. `internal/tui/msgs.go`: `CatalogRefreshedMsg` gains `Cfg *config.Config`. `internal/tui/root.go`: `Root`/`Options` gain `catalogRefreshFor`/`CatalogRefreshFor`, wired through `NewRoot`; `applyCatalogRefreshed`'s signature changed to take the whole `CatalogRefreshedMsg` (not just `*catalog.Catalog`) so it can also apply `Cfg`, with the in-place-copy logic described above. `internal/tui/login.go`: `finishLogin`'s success path now chains `refreshCatalogCmd` via `tea.Batch` alongside `cancelLoginWith`'s own cmd when `catalogRefreshFor` is wired; a nil factory (every other test in this package, any caller with nothing wired) falls back to the pre-F2 behaviour unchanged. `internal/app/catalogrefresh.go` (new): `NewCatalogRefreshFactory(version string) tui.CatalogRefreshFactory` — the real implementation, closed over `version` only (deliberately not `cfg`, since the whole point is that the cfg it discovers against cannot be the one captured at boot): each call re-reads `config.Load(config.Options{UserPath: xdg.ConfigFile()})` fresh, then `LoadCatalog`/`BackgroundRefresh` against that reloaded config — a discovery failure or `config.Load` error reports as `(nil, nil)`, a no-op `applyCatalogRefreshed` already handles safely, rather than surfacing as a crash or erasing the config the wizard's own success line already promised. `internal/app/app.go`: wires `CatalogRefreshFor: NewCatalogRefreshFactory(version)` into `tui.NewRoot`'s `Options`. **Tests.** Two new tests in `internal/tui/login_internal_test.go`: `TestFinishLoginSuccessChainsCatalogRefresh` (a fake `catalogRefreshFor` closure proves the returned cmd — batched or direct — eventually produces a `CatalogRefreshedMsg` carrying exactly the catalog/config the factory returned) and `TestFinishLoginSuccessNoCatalogRefreshFactoryFallsBack` (nil factory, the pre-F2 behaviour, no panic). **Verification.** `gofmt -l .` clean (after two `gofmt -w` passes, on `internal/tui/root.go` and `internal/app/app.go`, both pre-existing struct-literal alignment gofmt itself flagged — no semantic change); `go build ./...` clean; `go vet ./...` clean; full `go test ./...` green across all packages, including `internal/tui` (~68s) and `internal/app` — plus the five §6.1 boundary tests (`TestTUINoImportaHTTP`, `TestProviderNoImportaPresentacion`, `TestConvoEsPuro`, `TestEngineNoImportaProvider`, `TestToolsNoImportaTUI`) re-run explicitly and still passing, confirming `internal/tui` referencing `*config.Config` values directly (already precedented by `Root.cfg`/`Options.Cfg`) does not reopen that boundary, since the actual disk-reading `config.Load` call and the network-touching `RefreshCatalog`/`BackgroundRefresh` call stay on the `internal/app` side, reached only through the new function-typed seam. **This closes F2 in full** (both the hot-apply fix and the already-satisfied omniroute-in-selection-list confirmation) but **does not close W4**: per "no wave/sub-item closes piecemeal," `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md`'s W4 status block stays untouched until F5 (scoped-models), F10 (invert provider-add verification default), F11 (row format), and F9's model-side needs also land. **Operational note:** this window's sandbox reset mid-session (a fresh clone with no Go toolchain, immediately after the previous window's uncommitted work — which had never made it into a real commit yet — was lost), so the whole slice (design plus code plus tests) was redone from scratch against `origin/genspark_ai_developer`'s actual head; recovered via the standard `curl`/`tar` install of `go1.27.0` to `/usr/local/go`, confirmed `origin/main`/`origin/genspark_ai_developer` unchanged in the interim via `git fetch`. **A near-miss worth recording so it does not recur:** immediately before redoing the work, a `git commit --amend --no-edit` was run without first confirming which branch `HEAD` was on — it landed on `main` (already at `origin/main`'s merged tip, since the branch checkout that should have preceded it had not actually happened yet) rather than a feature branch; caught immediately via `git reflog`/`git log` showing an unexpected single-commit history, corrected with `git reset --hard origin/main` before anything was pushed, with zero actual loss (main was never pushed in the bad state). Files: `internal/tui/{catalogrefresh.go (new), msgs.go, root.go, login.go, login_internal_test.go}`, `internal/app/{catalogrefresh.go (new), app.go}`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |

A standalone `config.Load()` smoke test (written, run, and discarded — not committed, since it duplicates existing `internal/config` coverage) confirmed `defaults.toml`'s new section round-trips into `CatalogCurate` correctly before this entry was written. **Verification.** `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` clean, full `go test ./...` green across all 29 packages (~80s) — including every pre-existing `internal/app`/`internal/config` test, unmodified, still passing (the new `[catalog.curate]` defaults are all `false` in the test helper's hand-built `config.Catalog{}` literals, so no existing fixture accidentally starts getting models hidden out from under it). Two real bugs were found and fixed on the way: (1) `Model` (internal/catalog/model.go) had no `Modalities []string` or `Temperature *bool` fields at all, even though `nonChat()`'s three-signal disjunction (design doc §1.2) needs both — added both, right after `MaxOutput int`, with doc comments spelling out that empty/nil means "unknown, never a reason to hide" (principle 10), not false; (2) `modelsdev.go`'s `digest()` was wiring `MDModel.Modalities` from `w.Modalities.Input` — the wrong side; Layer 1's modality signal is specifically about OUTPUT modality (a model that cannot produce text, e.g. Veo/Imagen/TTS), so fixed to `w.Modalities.Output`, confirmed via grep this was the only consumer of the old (buggy) value. `merge.go`'s `applyModelsDev` then got a small copy-only-if-unset block carrying both new fields from `MDModel` to `Model`, inserted right before the existing `Status`→tag switch. New file `internal/catalog/curate.go` (~280 lines) implements Layer 1 close to verbatim against the design doc: `Rules` (`ChatOnly`, `HideDeprecated`, `HideSuperseded`, `HideDatedTwins`, `HideLatest`, global `Hide`/`Keep` globs, per-provider `Providers map[string]ProviderRules`), `Reason` (9 constants), `Hidden{Model, Reason}`, and `Curate(cat Catalog, r Rules) (kept Catalog, hidden []Hidden)` — a pure function, never mutating its input, building a per-provider lowercase-WireID set once up front so the two relational rules can check "does the base/undated sibling exist in this same provider" in O(1). `decide()` centralizes ordering: an explicit `Keep` glob (global or per-provider) wins first and unconditionally, ahead of even the `usedOrDeclared` carve-out (`UseCount > 0 || Source.Has(SourceConfig)`, generalized from `merge.go`'s pre-existing `HideDeprecated`-only carve-out to every rule here); then, only for models that are neither kept-by-glob nor used/declared, `HideDeprecated` → `ChatOnly`'s `nonChat()` (modality-lacks-text / `MaxOutput==1` / `Temperature!=nil && !*Temperature && !Tools && !JSONSchema`, each treating nil/zero/empty as "unknown, keep" per principle 10) → `HideSuperseded` (`X-preview`/`X-experimental`/`X-exp` hidden only if base `X` exists in the *same* provider, via `isSuperseded`/`stripSupersededSuffix`) → `HideDatedTwins` (`X-<date>` hidden only if undated `X` exists in the same provider, reusing `NormalizeID`'s own `dateSuffix` regexp) → `HideLatest` (off by default; | 2026-08-21 | W2 (part 1) · streaming agent-turn API in `internal/engine` — **W2 item 1 of 5, not yet closed: TUI wiring (items 2-5) not started** | First implementation slice of W2 ("The turn stops blocking", DECISION-2), started immediately after W3 closed and merged (PR #194, prior entry below). Per the roadmap's own internal ordering for this wave ("eventing first, then the UI affordances that depend on it"), this slice is item 1 only: `internal/engine.RunAgentTurnStreaming`, the streaming sibling DECISION-2 asks for, with `RunAgentTurn`'s existing blocking form explicitly preserved byte-for-byte (§12bis's own closing criterion — `internal/app`'s headless/serve paths depend on it, and neither was touched). **Design.** Rather than duplicate §12bis's six semantics (hard cap, loop detection, cancellation, error-is-data, output truncation, refusal-ends-the-turn) into a second ~500-line copy of the loop — the exact "no second copy" reasoning `engine.Engine.open`'s own doc comment already applies to the handshake-retry policy — `RunAgentTurn` and the new `RunAgentTurnStreaming` are now two thin public entry points over one shared private body, `runAgentTurn(ctx, req, opts, history, sink *AgentSink)`: `RunAgentTurn` calls it with `sink == nil`, `RunAgentTurnStreaming` with a non-nil one. Every event-reporting call site in the loop guards on `sink != nil` (and, per field, on that specific callback being non-nil) before firing, so a nil sink costs the blocking path nothing beyond those checks — confirmed by `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingMatchesBlockingForm`, which runs the identical script through both entry points and asserts identical `AgentResult` and history growth. **The new `AgentSink` type** (`agentloop.go`) carries six fields, each independently optional (nil means "not called," mirroring `AgentOptions.OnWait`'s existing contract) and each doc-commented with its own ordering guarantee: `OnTextDelta`/`OnReasoningDelta` (fire per-delta, in arrival order, exactly what `AgentResult.Text`/`.Reasoning` eventually concatenate to — proven live, not just at turn-end, by `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingReportsTextAndReasoningDeltasLive`); `OnToolCallStart`/`OnToolCallEnd` (Start fires only for a call that already passed the cap/loop-detection checks for its batch, so a caller never sees a Start with no matching End; End fires only after that call's `BlockToolResult`/`BlockToolErrorResult` is already in history — proven, including the exact history length at the instant End fires, by `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingReportsToolCallStartAndEnd` — and wired into all six terminal paths a tool call can take: cancelled before starting, no runner bound, cancelled mid-runner-call, a human refusal via `deniedHint`, and the two ordinary success/failure outcomes); `OnUsage` (fires on every running-total update, mirroring `StreamBuf.setUsage`'s own "either call overwrites, never a delta" contract); `OnPhase` (fires `"exec"` once per loop iteration — W2 item 2's "phase/footer updates from real events rather than inferred ones" — proven at exactly 2 firings for a one-tool-call-then-answer turn, i.e. two iterations, by `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingReportsPhaseExecPerIteration`; `AgentOptions.OnWait` remains the separate, unchanged source for the "wait `<duration>`" phase). **The steering hook, `Inject func() []convo.Message`**, is DECISION-2 consequence 2's own mechanism (W2 item 4): polled once per iteration, at the very top — after the previous iteration's own messages already landed in history, before that iteration's request is rebuilt from `history.Active()` — so whatever it returns joins history in time for the model's very next request to already see it in context, exactly like any other user message (`root.go`'s own submit's "the request is the history" discipline, reapplied here one level down). `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingInjectAddsMessageBeforeNextRequest` proves this by inspecting the *second* iteration's own recorded request (via `scriptedStreamer.requestAt`) and finding the injected text already present in its `Messages`, not merely somewhere in the final history once the turn ended. **The W2 gate — explicitly named as such in the roadmap, not a code-review note.** DECISION-2 states a steering message "must never widen permissions: cannot approve a pending tool call, cannot change autonomy level, cannot cancel a §21.4 invariant," and requires "a test asserting the negative case… before W2 can be considered closed." `TestRunAgentTurnStreamingInjectCannotApprovePendingToolCall` is that test: a `Runner` that blocks (mirroring `permissions.Guard.Authorize`'s own real block-on-`Reply` shape while `ModeToolApprove` is open) is held open by a second goroutine while `Inject` is polled and returns a steering message; the assertion is structural, not timing-based — `AgentSink` has no field, channel, or side path that could reach a `Runner` call already in flight, because `Inject` is only ever read once, at the top of the *next* iteration, which cannot begin until the current one's tool call has already returned. The test confirms the tool's own result in history is exactly what the (real, unblocked) `Runner` produced with no trace of the steering text, and that the steering message's own history position is strictly *after* the pending call's result — i.e. it could not have influenced a decision that had already resolved before the steering message could even be considered. This passes today, before any TUI-side steering feature exists, because the property is enforced by `engine`'s own structure (no code path reads `Inject` while a tool call is in flight) rather than by application-level policy that a later feature could accidentally bypass. **Tests.** New file `internal/engine/agentstream_test.go`, six tests: the blocking-form-equivalence test, the two live-delta tests, the phase test, the injection-ordering test, and the security-gate test above. **Verification.** `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` OK, full `go test ./...` green across all 29 packages (`internal/engine` 0.9s, `internal/tui` ~68s) and `go test ./internal/engine/... -race` green including every new and pre-existing test. **What did not land this slice, on purpose.** Items 2-5 of W2 (TUI event consumption/live reasoning and real phase display; non-modal `ModeBusy` and its `esc` re-scoping with the required §13 doc update; the steering+follow-up-queue UI and its two config keys, which is where the negative-assertion test above actually gets exercised end to end through a real `ModeToolApprove` dialog rather than a fake blocking `Runner`; the unified reasoning+code fold toggle) are unstarted — `internal/tui` was not touched at all this slice, deliberately, so this entry describes `internal/engine` work only. Per the roadmap's own "no wave closes piecemeal" rule, W2's status block in `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md` is not touched until all five items are genuinely closed together. **Operational note, same recurring pattern.** The Go toolchain was again absent at the start of this slice; recovered via `sudo apt-get install -y golang-go` + `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` auto-downloading the `go.mod`-pinned `go1.26.5`. | 2026-08-21 | CI fix · `askAndWait`'s post-Enter race (PR #194, following the part-6-closing entry below) — **not a W3/roadmap step; a CI-only test-harness fix, needed before #194 can merge** | PR #194's `build · vet · fmt · test` job failed on GitHub's real runner: `TestB4bFullscreenLosesNoContentAcrossAResizeCycle` reported `"DOSMARCA"` truncated to `"OSMARCA"` on the grid — read at first as possible real content loss, but reproduced locally at a ~5-10% rate under `GOMAXPROCS=1` contention (30-100-iteration stress loops), which pointed at a timing race rather than the mechanism under test. **Investigated as a possible real defect first**, per this project's standing "no quick fixes" rule. A disposable diagnostic test (`internal/tui/zzdiag_internal_test.go`, written, run, deleted — not part of the final diff) sent the second turn's marker one character at a time and dumped the grid after each: the very first character of the second marker was the one silently missing, not a truncation — meaning it was never inserted into the input box at all. Traced this to `ModeBusy`'s own `updateBusy` (`root.go`): any keypress other than the cancel binding is discarded outright while `m.mode == ModeBusy`, and a stray keystroke landing while the *first* turn's busy-to-chat transition was still in flight would be dropped exactly this way. **Root cause.** `askAndWait`'s shared helper (`regress_bugs_internal_test.go`) sends `Enter()` then calls `WaitWhile(busyWitness)`, relying on `Session.Settle()`'s "output went quiet" signal to mean "the program has caught up." bubbletea v2's renderer runs on its own ticker, decoupled from `Update` — the exact same decoupling `Root.ExitTranscript`'s own doc comment already documents for a different seam (part 6's entry below) — so a turn fast enough to run `submit → ModeBusy → drainStream → finishTurn → ModeChat` between two ticks can flush only its *final* frame to the wire; the busy witness never appears at all, and `Settle()` reports quiet the instant that one frame lands. `WaitWhile` is then trivially satisfied by a frame that already looks "done" on screen while `finishTurn`'s own tail (`checkEndOfTurn`, `releaseTurn`) may not have fully returned inside the model, so the very next `Type()` call from the following `askAndWait` can race a keystroke into a `ModeBusy` window that has no visible witness on screen at all — there is no string this harness could watch for that would prove "the model has finished unwinding," since that state is purely internal. Confirmed by an instrumented diagnostic that logged `Grid` state at 20ms intervals immediately after the first turn's `Enter()`: the busy witness appeared and cleared within a single ~20ms window on a fast machine, well inside a window `Settle()`'s 30ms quiet threshold can miss entirely. **Fix.** `askAndWait` now calls `s.Settle()` a second time immediately after `WaitWhile` returns — mirroring `Session.Quit()`'s own existing comment ("Settling once more keeps the guarantee even if a renderer flushes asynchronously") — giving the one guaranteed synchronization point (quiet output) one more chance to reassert itself after whatever frame satisfied `WaitWhile` was drawn, so a caller's next `Type()` cannot race ahead of a transition still landing. This is a minimal, surgical change to a single ~20-year-old (in this codebase's terms) shared helper, not a new wait primitive, on the theory that the existing "wait for quiet, twice" idiom used at shutdown generalizes cleanly to this earlier point in a session's lifetime. **Verification of the fix, not just the report.** `GOMAXPROCS=1 go test ./internal/tui/... -run TestB4bFullscreenLosesNoContentAcrossAResizeCycle -count=30` — 30/30 pass (previously ~5-10% failure rate at the same contention level, reproduced repeatedly before the fix). Full `gofmt -l .` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go build ./...` OK, `go test ./...` green across all 29 packages (`internal/tui` ~68s). **What was not changed.** No application code (`root.go`, `view.go`, `app.go`) — the busy-line-drop behavior in `updateBusy` is correct and intentional (§7.4's "input has no meaning while a turn generates"); the defect was entirely in the test harness's own synchronization, not in anything a real terminal user could trigger (a real keyboard cannot type faster than a human, and this race needs sub-millisecond back-to-back submits only an automated harness produces). **Honesty about the fix's limits.** A second `Settle()` closes the specific gap this investigation reproduced and stress-tested, but — consistent with `WaitFor`'s own comment on the mid-stream tick-gap race and its 20s-deadline entry's own admission that raising a number "does not provably eliminate" a scheduling race — this is not a formal proof the gap can never reopen under worse contention than reproduced here; if it recurs, the honest next step named in that same spirit is a real state-based witness (e.g. exposing `Root.mode` through a debug-only accessor) rather than a third `Settle()` call. Files: `internal/tui/regress_bugs_internal_test.go`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |

Fixed by switching the count/order assertions to short, single-word markers (`"UNOMARCA"`, `"DOSMARCA"`) and adding one separate, deliberately long third prompt reserved only for the width-wrap invariant (`s.Grid().Widest()`). | 2026-08-21 | W3 (part 6, in progress) · fullscreen emit path: `AltScreen=true`, DECISION-1b's exit transcript, `evictOverflow`'s fullscreen guard — **W3 still not closed: §4.1 assertions 3/6 tests not yet written** | Sixth implementation slice of W3, directly continuing part 5's `/hotkeys` overlay (previous entry below, PR #192/`12a3232`) and the immediately preceding CI fix (also below, `1859b64`, merged), picking up the one genuinely open design question the prior turn's investigation had converged on but not concluded: how to make `emit`'s `fullscreen` branch actually set `AltScreen = true` — closing part of docs/DESIGN-tui-mode.md §4 Rule 2's own "NOT YET IMPLEMENTED" stub — without silently breaking DECISION-1b's exit-transcript guarantee the moment it did. **The investigation, and its conclusion.** Read charm.land/bubbletea/v2@v2.0.9's own source (not inferred from its doc comments, which turned out to be misleading on this exact point) end to end along the relevant path: `cursedRenderer.render(v)` (`cursed_renderer.go:581-586`) does nothing but `s.view = v` — zero I/O. The bytes that make up a frame only reach the real terminal on an *independent* clock: `Program.startRenderer` (`tea.go:1391-1417`) runs a `time.NewTicker(framerate)` loop calling `p.flush()`/`renderer.flush(false)` on every tick, completely decoupled from the Update/View cycle any `tea.Cmd` runs inside. Meanwhile `insertAbove` — what `tea.Println` actually calls (`cursed_renderer.go:711`) — writes synchronously into whichever screen buffer the renderer's own bookkeeping currently says is active, with **no altscreen guard actually present in the code** despite `renderer.go`'s own doc comment claiming one exists ("If the altscreen is active no output will be printed") — a real discrepancy between doc and code, confirmed by reading `nil_renderer.go` too (also no guard, trivially, since it does nothing at all). Consequently: any design that sequences "print the transcript, then quit" from *inside* the running `tea.Program` — `tea.Sequence(printCmd, tea.Quit)`, or forcing `AltScreen=false` on the quit-confirming `Update` before sequencing the print — is **provably racy, not merely awkward**: the print and the real AltScreen-exit write can land on either order on the wire, non-deterministically, and on the losing order the exit transcript is written into the doomed alternate-screen buffer instead of persistent scrollback, silently defeating DECISION-1b. The one deterministic synchronization point is `Program.Run()` itself returning: its tail (`tea.go:1144-1171`) unconditionally calls `p.shutdown(killed)` → `p.stopRenderer(kill)` (`tea.go:1427`) → (unless killed) `renderer.flush(true)` then unconditionally `renderer.close()` (`cursed_renderer.go:144`, which synchronously writes and flushes `ansi.ResetModeAltScreenSaveCursor` when the last `View` had `AltScreen == true`) → `p.restoreTerminalState()` (`tty.go:33`) — all of which happens strictly before `Run()` returns control to its caller. **The resulting design.** `Root.ExitTranscript() string` (`view.go`) is a plain method — not a `tea.Cmd`, never called from anywhere inside this package's own `Update`/`View` — that renders the *entire* `m.transcript` (every entry, not just `[printedUpTo:]`, since `printedUpTo` never advances in fullscreen — see below) at the frame's own content width. `internal/app.Run` (`app.go`) is the one caller: `final, err := p.Run()` now captures the final `tea.Model`, and after the existing error check, `if root, ok := final.(tui.Root); ok { if t := root.ExitTranscript(); t != "" { fmt.Print(t) } }` — a plain `fmt.Print`, never `tea.Println`, since by then there is no running `Program` left to hand a `Cmd` to. Both `Options.FullscreenExitTranscript` (new field, `root.go`, wired from `cfg.UI.FullscreenExitTranscript` — already existing config from part 1, previously unread) and `Root.exitTranscript` carry this unchanged, mirroring `TUIMode`/`Root.tuiMode`'s own three-hop pattern. **`emit`'s fullscreen branch itself** (`view.go`) shrank from a `switch`-with-`TODO` stub to one line: `v.AltScreen = mode == termenv.ModeFullscreen`. | 2026-08-20 | W1 (part 3) · RC-7 footer reflow policy — **closed, and with it W1 as a whole (see this entry's own tail)** | `RenderFooter` (`internal/tui/footer.go`) used to join every item with `"  "` and then remove items **right-to-left** the moment the single resulting line did not fit `lay.ContentWidth()` — the mechanism behind report **F14**: on a BPEstrecho terminal (40-59 columns, "Termux en vertical," this project's own most common real case per §9.1) that dropped `context`/`tokens`/`cost`/`git`/`cwd` entirely rather than using the second row `Layout.FooterSections()` already reserved for exactly this (`layout.go`, previously unused by `RenderFooter` — its own doc comment called it "reservado para la Fase 2 completa"). **What landed, in the order RC-7's roadmap section prescribed ("wrap to N rows, then abbreviate, then drop"):** `RenderFooter` now tries, for each right-truncated subset of the requested items (starting with all of them), `fitFooterItems`: render every item, then search from the widest per-item cap down to `footerMinAbbrevWidth` (3 columns — the least that can show one character plus path.go's own ellipsis) for the widest shared cap at which shrinking every item wider than that cap (via the new `abbreviateItem`, dispatching to `ShortenPath` for `cwd` and a glyph-preserving `truncateRunes` for `git`/everything else — deliberately reusing path.go's existing truncation patterns rather than inventing a second one) lets `wrapFooterRows` pack the result into at most `lay.FooterSections()` rows of at most `lay.ContentWidth()` columns each. Because lowering the cap only ever shrinks text further, fit is monotonic in the cap, so this search finds the *most* information that still fits, not just *some* fit. Only when no cap (down to the floor) makes a subset fit does the outer loop drop the last item and retry — the same right-to-left drop order as before, but now the last resort instead of the first response to any width. The lone exception to the floor: a subset of exactly one item is allowed to shrink to 1 column rather than be dropped to nothing, since there is nowhere else for it to go. `abbreviateItem`'s `git` case keeps the branch glyph and shrinks only the name (losing the glyph to an ellipsis first is a worse trade for one column of meaning). The result is `"\n"`-joined when wrapped to more than one row; `restRows()` (`view.go`, landed in part 2) already counted a multi-line `RenderFooter` output via `strings.Count(..., "\n")+1`, and `inputwrap_internal_test.go`'s `assertInputBoxMatchesTheWidget` already split on `"\n"` too, so RC-3's height-budget machinery and the input-box row-accounting test needed no changes at all to keep working with a wrapped footer — confirmed by the full suite staying green with no edits to either file. **Verified behaviour, probed directly rather than only inferred from the algorithm:** at width 45 (BPEstrecho, 2 rows) all six configured items (`model`/`context`/`tokens`/`cost`/`git`/`cwd`) now survive, wrapped across exactly two rows, where the old code would have dropped several; at width 40 with a pathologically long `cwd`, `ShortenPath` abbreviates it instead of the model/git items losing their turn; only at an extreme width (16 columns, BPMinimo, one row) does the last-resort drop still trigger, and even then the earliest, most-identity-bearing items (`model`/`context`/`tokens`) survive abbreviated while `cost`/`git`/`cwd` are what gets dropped — the opposite of information loss being total. **Tests.** `footer_test.go`'s `TestRenderFooterRecortaDeDerechaAIzquierdaSiNoEntra` — which locked in the old drop-first behaviour by name even though its own assertion (single line ≤ 20 runes) happened to still pass under the new code — was renamed to `TestRenderFooterNuncaExcedeElAnchoNiElNumeroDeFilas` and extended to also assert row count ≤ `lay.FooterSections()`, so its name no longer misdescribes what it guards. Three new tests: `TestRenderFooterEnvuelveEnVezDeSoltar` pins the BPEstrecho regression itself (all six items present across exactly 2 rows); `TestRenderFooterAbreviaAntesDeSoltar` pins the middle step (a too-long `cwd` comes back through `ShortenPath`, ending in its own leaf, while the model and git items are untouched); `TestRenderFooterSueltaSoloComoUltimoRecurso` pins the last-resort step at an extreme width (the earliest items survive abbreviated, `cost`/`git`/`cwd` are the ones actually dropped). All eight pre-existing footer tests (ASCII repertoire, nil-items default order, autonomy/phase drawing and omission) pass unchanged. **Not done in this change, on purpose.** The broader "every overlay reflows to the real width" rule the roadmap explicitly scopes to **W2** (`helpWidth = 38` hard-coded in `view.go`'s `renderHelp`) was left untouched — RC-7 is a W1 item, that hard-coded help width is not. No new glyph or abbreviation scheme was invented beyond what `path.go` already had; `footerMinAbbrevWidth` is a new constant but not a new *strategy*. **Verification.** `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go build ./...` OK, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` green across all 29 packages (`internal/tui` ~60s). **This closes W1 as a whole**: with part 1 (B3 real clear, `5288116`), part 2 (RC-3 height invariant/F20/RC-5 width invariant/one banner producer, `c3460fc`) and this part 3 (RC-7) all landed and green together, every acceptance criterion the roadmap's W1 section names now passes at once, satisfying the document's own "no wave starts/closes piecemeal" rule; `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md`'s W1 status note is updated accordingly in this same change. Files: `internal/tui/footer.go`, `internal/tui/footer_test.go`, `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |

Two sequential sessions a few hundred milliseconds apart normally land in the same wall-clock minute, but not always — when they straddle a minute boundary the header text genuinely differs even though the resize-cycle behaviour under test (wrap/duplicate/lose content) is byte-identical, producing a false failure that reproduces only probabilistically, exactly matching the CI asymmetry observed. Confirmed via `grep -n "testterm.Start"` that no other test in the file starts two independent sessions against each other, so none of the other B1-B4/RC-2/banner pins share this exposure. **Fix.** A `maskClock` helper (`regress_bugs_internal_test.go`): `hhmmRE = regexp.MustCompile(`\d{2}:\d{2}`)` replaces every `HH:MM`-shaped substring with `--:--` before the two renders are compared, so the assertion is on layout (no duplication, no loss, no stale wrap) rather than on which minute the test happened to execute in — it does not touch the harness, the renderer, or `time.Now()` anywhere in production code, since the nondeterminism is real (wall-clock time genuinely differs between two sequential sessions) and only the *assertion* needed to stop caring about it. **Verification:** `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go build ./...` OK, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` green across all 29 packages; `go test ./internal/tui/... -run TestB4ResizeCycleDoesNotCorruptTheScreen -v -count=3` passed 3/3 (~5.5s each) both before and after re-verifying the fix was correctly placed on `genspark_ai_developer` at `482fe75`. **Not in this change, on purpose.** No production code changed — `root.go`, `slashrun.go` and every other file from the W1-part-1/RC-2 commits are untouched; this is a test-assertion-only fix for a pre-existing flake, not a new behaviour. **An operational near-miss during this fix, recorded because it nearly caused real damage:** a sandbox reset mid-session reverted the checked-out branch back to `main` while leaving the uncommitted `maskClock` edit sitting in the working tree against the wrong base. While moving the fix onto the correct branch, a stale `/tmp` backup of the test file (taken earlier in the session, before the B3 hard-assertion promotion and before `TestRC2CursorStaysInsideTheInputWhileBusy` existed) was restored over the correctly-reset file — `git diff --stat` immediately showed an implausible 101-line diff, and inspecting it caught that it would have silently reverted B3's hard assertion back to a deferred pin *and deleted the entire RC-2 busy-mode test* had it been committed. Recovered via `git checkout --` to discard the bad restore, then re-derived the `maskClock` edit directly from a fresh `Read` of the actual current file rather than trusting the cached copy — `git diff --stat` (19 insertions/3 deletions) and `grep -c "func Test"` (11, unchanged) confirmed the correct, minimal result before this entry was written. Files: `internal/tui/regress_bugs_internal_test.go`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |

The deliverable is the gate document that condition demands. **The decisions, as recorded in `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md` (each now carrying an `ANSWERED` block):** `DECISION-1` dual mode **approved** (`regular` on Termux, `fullscreen` on desktop/compatible), which formally **reopens** §3's twice-CLOSED \"inline rendering stays, as-is, with no reflow\"; `DECISION-1b` **approved** — dump the conversation to real scrollback on `fullscreen` exit; `DECISION-2` all three contract consequences **approved**; `DECISION-3` **decided against my recommendation** — `google` becomes the *real internal identifier*, a full rename of `gemini-direct` including migrations, references, tests, config and documentation (*\"sigue siendo un proyecto interno y tenemos tiempo para hacerlo correctamente\"*), so the label-only proposal is overruled and withdrawn; wave order **`W0→W1→W3→W2→W4→W5→W6`** — the *alternative* I offered, i.e. visual corruption relieved before blocked input. Two gating rules were attached and are recorded as rules, not intentions: `W0` stays a pure harness that changes no behaviour, and no wave starts until the previous one's acceptance criteria and tests pass. A knowingly-accepted cost of `W3`-before-`W2`: **`F8b`'s payoff is deferred**, since its \"expand old code blocks\" half needs `W3`'s viewport *and* `W2`'s event stream, so the rendering half lands first and sits inert. **The dependency question, answered with evidence rather than reassurance.** Headline finding: **nothing new is added — not one module, not one build tag, not one C dependency; `go.mod` is untouched by `W0`, `W1` and `W3`**, verified with `git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum`. The load-bearing fact, found by reading the vendored source rather than the docs, is that **`tea.View.AltScreen` is a plain `bool` field on the value `View()` returns** — in Bubble Tea v2 the alternate screen is neither a separate renderer nor a program option, so `fullscreen` is a field assignment, not a second rendering stack. Every remaining `fullscreen` need (wrapping, erase-display, scroll region, colour capability, size) maps onto an already-**direct** dependency: `charmbracelet/x/ansi` (`Wrap`/`Hardwrap`, `EraseEntireDisplay`/`EraseEntireScrollback`), `x/term`, `colorprofile`, `lipgloss/v2`. Third-party VT emulators and pty drivers were considered and **rejected on Termux grounds specifically**, not on taste: a pty means CGO, and CGO is precisely what is already delicate there. **The harness claim was probed empirically, not asserted** — a disposable program under `/tmp` (deleted afterwards, never part of the repo) ran a real `tea.Program` with `WithInput`/`WithOutput` on two `bytes.Buffer`s, `WithWindowSize(20,6)` and `WithEnvironment([\"TERM=xterm-256color\"])`, producing 91 bytes which `ansi.Parser` then decoded into `Print` (\"HELLO\"/\"WORLD\"), `Execute` (`\\r`, `\\n`) and 12 CSI commands including `CSI-J`. That settles three things at once: Bubble Tea renders happily to a non-TTY writer so **no pty and no CGO are needed**; `ansi.Handler`'s `Print`/`Execute`/`HandleCsi` trio is exactly the surface a cell grid needs; and injected input really does drive the model, so the `B1`/`B4` regression scripts are writable. It also surfaced a design constraint that would have been easy to get wrong: the renderer emits `\\r` + `ESC[J` with **relative** cursor movement, so the test grid must model terminal-side auto-wrap honestly — **a grid that \"fixes\" wrapping while parsing would hide the very bug it exists to catch**. **Detection was designed as a package, not an `if`**, because the owner explicitly refused the shortcut *\"No asumas simplemente que 'WSL = regular'\"*. The reframing that makes it tractable: **WSL is not a terminal, it is a kernel interface** — so detection answers two orthogonal questions, `Platform` (where the process runs) and `Host` (what actually draws our bytes), and **mode is decided by `Host`**, with `Platform` only ever a tie-breaker. WSL under Windows Terminal or tmux therefore gets `fullscreen`; WSL under bare legacy conhost gets `regular`. New pure package `internal/termenv` (imports limited to `os`, `runtime`, `strings`, `path/filepath`, `io`, with its own purity guard added to `internal/arch_test.go`), modelled directly on `theme.DiagnoseEnv`'s injectable precedent and **reusing `xdg.IsTermux()` rather than duplicating it**; `DetectEnv(override, goos, env, tty, probe)` returns `Detection{Mode, Platform, Host, Reason, Signals, Advice}`, with filesystem access confined to an injected `Probe{KernelRelease, Exists}` so every rule is exercisable from a table test. 13 worked scenarios are written out and become those tests, honouring the §17-recurring principle that **\"a rule that can only be exercised by shipping it is not a rule.\"** **The anti-fragility constraint** (*\"no una excusa para mantener dos implementaciones frágiles\"*) is discharged by a single seam: `render(state, width, height) -> Frame` is **shared and forbidden to know the mode at all**, and `emit(Frame, mode) -> (bytes, committed)` is the **only** mode-aware function in the tree; resize never patches, it rebuilds from state. Six harness assertions pin it, including mode-invariant content, shrink→shrink→grow→grow idempotence, \"one banner ever\", and the exit transcript — which `DECISION-1b` promotes from a nicety to a `W3` gate: every committed turn, in order, exactly once. **`DECISION-3`'s migration plan, since a rename of a persisted id is a data migration and not a find-and-replace:** a **permanent** read-time alias `gemini-direct → google` (not a deprecation window — old session JSONL files are historical records and must stay readable indefinitely); a one-shot idempotent, backed-up write migration for `config.toml` and the credentials store (`internal/config/credentials.go:129`); **session JSONL never rewritten in place**, because a migration that rewrites history is how a transcript gets corrupted; and a test that asserts the *alias*, not merely the rename. Scheduled for `W5`, deliberately not in flight while the renderer is rebuilt. **A real defect of my own was found and fixed while here:** an unescaped `&#124;` inside a §17 table cell breaks the row, and one had already shipped in merged PR #181 (this table, the entry below, 4 columns where the header has 3). Found by writing an escape-aware column validator that splits rows on *unescaped* pipes only; the first fix attempt **reintroduced the bug**, because backslash-escaping fails when the same cell also quotes a backslash — the `&#124;` entity is the unambiguous form and is now the rule for this file. The validator also flagged **11 pre-existing broken rows elsewhere in `PLAN.md`, deliberately left untouched**, so an unrelated cosmetic repair cannot hide a planning change in the same diff. **Verification:** the sandbox reset again mid-session (Go toolchain gone, *both* of the session's commits vanished — `git cat-file -t` on each returned \"not a valid object name\" — and only merged PR #181's content survived), so the ROADMAP annotations and this entry were written twice; recovered by reinstalling `go1.26.5`, cutting a fresh branch from `origin/main` at `eaeb873`, and redoing the lost edits. `go build ./...` clean; `gofmt -l internal cmd` clean; `git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum` clean — the document's central claim held under test. **Status: `W0` does not begin until this gate document is agreed.** Files: `docs/DESIGN-tui-mode.md` (new), `docs/ROADMAP-ux-2026-08-20.md` (ANSWERED blocks for all four decisions, approved wave order, §6.1 answers table), `docs/PLAN.md` (this entry, plus the broken-row fix in the entry below). |

| 2026-08-19 | UX bug report · the model's internal reasoning never appears — **closed** (nobody was ever *asking* the service for it) | Closes the sixth and final reported issue from the 2026-08-18 "model picker" batch, whose two previous entries below built the engine-layer plumbing (`AgentResult.Reasoning`) and the TUI render layer (grey preview, ~2 lines, expandable). The user reported, with a pasted live transcript, that they still saw no reasoning at all: under `omniroute/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` strings like `**Defining the Query**` leaked into the *answer body*, and after switching to `gemini-direct/models/gemini-3.6-flash` no reasoning showed up on any turn. **Root cause, confirmed by reading every layer end to end plus Google's own API documentation:** the rendering pipeline built by the two entries below is complete and correct — the bug sits at the opposite end of the pipe. Gemini thought summaries are **opt-in on the request**: the service returns nothing thought-marked unless the caller says it wants it, and no adapter in this codebase ever said so. Three layers were each individually "correct" while the composed feature produced literally zero output: (a) the native adapter (`internal/provider/gemini`) never sent `generationConfig.thinkingConfig.includeThoughts`, which made `emitPart`'s already-written `case part.Thought:` branch unreachable dead code; (b) the OpenAI-compatible adapter — which is the user's *actual* path, since `internal/config/credentials.go`'s `gemini` preset yields `{ID: "gemini-direct", Kind: "openai"}` and talks to Google's compat shim — never sent the top-level `extra_body.google.thinking_config.include_thoughts`, and, just as importantly, never *read* the response marker either; (c) `internal/app` had no notion of reasoning in the request at all, so `config.UI.Reasoning` (`off`/`collapsed`/`full`) only ever gated *rendering* of data that was never requested. The shim's response shape is the subtle part and also explains the omniroute leak the user saw: on the compat shim the thought summary arrives in the **ordinary `content` field**, distinguished *only* by `extra_content.google.thought` (Google's docs: it "explicitly marks if a field is a thought and takes precedence over `thought_tag_marker`"), and without the optional `thought_tag_marker` request field "no tags will be returned around the model's thoughts" — so any client that ignores `extra_content` necessarily renders the reasoning as answer prose, exactly the `**Defining the Query**` symptom. Also documented while here (and deliberately *not* used): `reasoning_effort` controls how *much* the model thinks, never whether the narration comes back, and cannot be combined with `thinking_config`. **Fix, in four commits, one per architectural seam:** (1) `provider.Request` gains `IncludeReasoning bool` — the contract distinction between "the model thinks" and "the service narrates its thinking", with `false` keeping every existing request byte-for-byte identical on the wire; (2) the native adapter's `buildBody` sets `gc.ThinkingConfig = &wireThinkingConfig{IncludeThoughts: true}` when asked (new `wireGenConfig.ThinkingConfig` field, and the inner bool deliberately carries **no** `omitempty` so `includeThoughts: true` always serialises); (3) the OpenAI adapter sends the `extra_body` opt-in — **host-gated** behind a new `isGoogleHost(p.base)` so Google-specific fields can never leak to `api.openai.com` or a third-party gateway — and both stream pumps (`pumpSSE` and the non-streaming `pumpWhole`) now classify content as `provider.EventReasoning` instead of `EventDelta` when `extra_content.google.thought` is set, via a new nil-safe `(*wireExtraContent).thought()` accessor; (4) `internal/app` gains `ReasoningWanted(cfg)` (`ui.reasoning != "off"`, nil-safe, case/space-insensitive) and threads it through `NewStreamer`'s new third parameter into `Request.IncludeReasoning` at *every* door: `BuildEngine`, `NewEngineFactory`, `headless.go`, `serve.go`, and `agentturn.go` — the last of which inherits `req.IncludeReasoning` from its parent turn rather than re-reading config, so a sub-agent can never disagree with the turn that spawned it. **15 new tests** across three packages (`internal/provider/gemini/thinking_test.go` ×4 with a new `stream_pensamiento.sse` fixture carrying `thought:true` parts and `thoughtsTokenCount:40`; `internal/provider/openai/thinking_test.go` ×6 with `stream_pensamiento_google.sse`; `internal/app/reasoning_test.go` ×5), each proven non-vacuous by mutation: disabling the native opt-in, dropping the Google host gate (caught `extra_body` leaking to `api.openai.com`), ignoring the `thought` flag (reproduced the user's leak symptom exactly), and hard-coding `false` in both `BuildEngine` and `NewEngineFactory` all made their own tests fail, as did treating an unset `ui.reasoning` as `off`. **Lesson worth recording:** the first draft of the app-layer test passed under mutation because it *replicated* `BuildEngine`'s two wiring lines instead of calling `BuildEngine` — precisely the "each half tested on its own side of the seam" flaw that let the original bug ship in the first place. It was rewritten around a synthetic provider kind registered via `provider.Register` that captures the real `provider.Request`, so the assertions now drive the actual assembly functions; a second mutation attempt also silently no-oped against stale line numbers before being corrected, which is why every mutation here was re-checked against `grep` output rather than trusted line offsets. **Explicitly not changed:** no TUI file was touched — the render layer from the two entries below needed no fix; `provider.CapsFor` still leaves `Caps.Reasoning` unset (it is not consulted on this path, and inferring it per-model is a separate question); the `thought_tag_marker` request field is left unsent since `extra_content.google.thought` is authoritative and takes precedence. **Verification:** sandbox reset three times during the work (Go toolchain gone, branch reverted to `main` each time) — recovered by reinstalling `go1.26.5` and re-checking out the branch from `origin`, with no committed work ever lost thanks to pushing after every commit. `gofmt -l .` clean; `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green across all 27 packages; `go test -race ./internal/tui/... ./internal/app/...` green (`internal/tui` 22.2s, `internal/app` 8.6s). | 2026-08-19 | UX bug report · user messages should have a distinct background colour (part of the sixth issue, "show reasoning + user message background + remaining terminal bugs") — **closed** | Second half of the batch's sixth and final reported issue, split from its "show ~2 lines of reasoning" sibling (tracked separately, not yet started) because the two touch unrelated parts of the rendering pipeline and the fix's own risk — see below — was substantial enough to deserve its own verification pass. The 2026-08-19 entry immediately below this one ("user/assistant messages are not visually differentiated") had already coloured each bubble's *header* (marker/name/timestamp) by role via `styles.User`/`styles.Assistant` foreground colours; this report explicitly asks for something distinct from that — a different **background** behind the user's whole message, not just a coloured header line. **New theme data:** `Theme.UserBG RGB` (`internal/theme/theme.go`), wired through `builtinFallback()` (`#182420`, a dark desaturated tint of `User`'s own `#7fd1b9` teal rather than the bright accent itself — painted solid behind a paragraph of `#e8e6e3` text, the teal would be louder than every other surface in the interface) and through `parse()`'s `targets` map (`user_bg` TOML key) the same way every other colour already is, so an old theme file that predates this field still gets a sensible dark default rather than `RGB{}`'s pure black — `ascua.toml` itself gained the matching `user_bg = "#182420"` line. **The central technical risk, found by reading `charmbracelet/x/ansi`'s vendored source directly:** lipgloss v2's `Style.Styled()` (the method every `.Render()` call bottoms out in) always appends a *full* SGR reset (`ansi.ResetStyle`, `"\x1b[m"`) after its own content — not one scoped to the single attribute it just set. A user message's body routinely contains other already-`.Render()`-ed runs nested inside it (a fenced code block's own Chroma-per-token colouring, `codeblock.go`'s `highlightSource`), each ending in this same full reset — so naively wrapping the whole body in `bg.Render(body)` would only paint the background up to the *first* such nested reset; everything after it would silently lose the background and fall back to the terminal's own default, which is a real, demonstrated failure mode (confirmed with a disposable scratch reproduction under `/tmp`, not part of this repo) rather than a theoretical concern. `Style.Width(n)` was also tried and rejected: it does correctly pad trailing space with the background colour, but the same mid-line nested-reset bug still applies to the actual text content, and forcing every line to a fixed width pads even the last line with unwanted trailing space for what should read as "text on a coloured strip", not a padded box. Per-line splitting alone (`bg.Render(line)` for each `\n`-delimited line) was tried too and does **not** sidestep the problem either — the nested-reset issue reproduces within a single line regardless of whether the background is applied once around the whole block or once per line. **The fix**, `Styles.PaintBackground(block string) string` (`internal/theme/style.go`): probes `UserBG`'s own rendered escape codes by rendering a single NUL byte and splitting on it (so the exact prefix/suffix bytes lipgloss would use are captured without hand-duplicating lipgloss's own SGR-building logic), then applies that prefix/suffix around each non-empty line by hand — critically, re-inserting the prefix immediately after every embedded `ansi.ResetStyle` found inside that line, so the background is re-established the instant an inner style's own reset would otherwise have cleared it. Blank lines are left untouched (a "coloured" empty line would still paint a visible strip of background across an otherwise-tight bubble, an odd cosmetic gap). Under `theme.CapNone` the probe's own prefix/suffix both come back empty (since `UserBG` itself is a colourless `lipgloss.NewStyle()` there, built by the same `plain` guard `NewStyles` already applies to every other field), so the whole function is a byte-for-byte no-op with no separate "if plain" branch needed — the same "no colour, ever" contract every other style in this package already honours. **Wiring:** `renderTranscriptLine` (`internal/tui/chat.go`) now calls `styles.PaintBackground` on the whole rendered bubble (header + body together, not the body alone) when `role == "user"`, so the background survives both the header's own `styles.User` foreground colouring and any code/prose styling in the body without losing the paint at their embedded resets. Assistant bubbles are left untouched — this is exclusively a user-message affordance, matching the reported ask. **`wrapText`'s own `ansi.Wrap`-based line wrapping was verified, not assumed, to preserve a background escape correctly across a wrap boundary** (a risk flagged as open in earlier planning): a scratch reproduction confirmed `ansi.Wrap` re-emits the leading background escape at the start of every wrapped line rather than only the first, so a long user message wrapping across several terminal rows keeps its background on every row, not just the first. **New tests:** `internal/theme/userbg_test.go` (new file) — `TestLoadEmbebidoUserBG` (the shipped `ascua.toml`'s own `user_bg` value parses correctly), `TestLoadUserThemeMissingUserBGFallsBackToBase` (a theme file that never sets `user_bg` inherits the base default rather than black), `TestLoadUserThemeCanOverrideUserBG` (a theme file's own `user_bg` wins, confirming the TOML key is actually wired into `parse`'s targets map and not merely declared on the struct), `TestPaintBackgroundSurvivesNestedReset` (the core regression: the background escape reappears after an embedded reset, so text following a nested styled run is not left unpainted), `TestPaintBackgroundNoColourIsNoOp` (`CapNone` returns the block byte-for-byte unchanged), `TestPaintBackgroundSkipsBlankLines` (an empty line inside a multi-line block stays empty rather than gaining a pointless escape pair). `internal/tui/chatstyle_internal_test.go` gained `TestRenderTranscriptLineUserGetsBackground` (a user bubble's header *and* body both carry the `UserBG` background escape; an assistant bubble carries neither) and `TestRenderTranscriptLineUserBackgroundSurvivesCodeBlock` (a user message containing a fenced, syntax-highlighted code block still shows the background escape reappearing after the code's own Chroma colouring, and the code text itself survives unchanged under the paint). **Scope note for whoever continues the batch:** the sixth issue's other half — showing ~2 lines of the model's "thinking"/reasoning stream, glued to the response in grey — remains open. Investigation this session found the underlying data-plumbing (`liveTurn.reason`/`appendReasoning`, `convo.Message.Reasoning()`, `config.UI.Reasoning`) already exists but is completely unwired into `internal/tui`, and — more importantly — that the tools-enabled agent-loop path (`internal/engine/agentloop.go`) structurally discards reasoning every iteration except on mid-turn cancellation, with no field on `AgentResult` to carry it even if captured; a real implementation needs a scope decision (plain-streaming-only vs. also extending `agentloop.go`) before it can start, and is left for the next entry in this file rather than folded into this one. **Verification:** sandbox had reset again since the previous session (Go toolchain missing, though this time the local `genspark_ai_developer` branch and its uncommitted `theme.go`/`ascua.toml` edits from the prior interrupted session both survived intact) — Go reinstalled (`go1.26.5`, matching `go.mod`); `gofmt -l .` clean; `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green across all 26 packages (one `[no test files]`); `go test -race ./internal/tui/...` green. Files: `internal/theme/theme.go`, `internal/theme/ascua.toml`, `internal/theme/style.go`, `internal/theme/userbg_test.go` (new), `internal/tui/chat.go`, `internal/tui/chatstyle_internal_test.go`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |

the body line, once stripped of ANSI, is untouched byte-for-byte), `TestRenderTranscriptLineNoColourEmitsNoEscape` (`theme.CapNone` still produces zero escape bytes, pinning the pre-existing contract against this exact change). **Verification:** sandbox had reset again since the previous session (Go toolchain missing, local git back on bare `main`) — Go reinstalled (`go1.26.5`); | 2026-08-19 | UX bug report · `/resume` drops tool activity from a past session — **closed** | Fourth of the batch of UX issues from the 2026-08-18 "model pasted a whole file" report: reopening a previous session (`--resume`, `resume_last`, or the in-session `/resume` menu) appeared to "not load all past messages". **Investigation ruled out the persistence layer first**, by reading `internal/convo/store.go` in full: `Store.Load`/`load` correctly reconstructs every message type from the JSONL, including `RoleTool` results — nothing is lost on disk, and every message does reach `conv.Messages` (the model's own context) intact. **Root cause, found via a scratch reproduction test** (written, run, then discarded — not part of the repo): `historyToTranscript` (`internal/tui/resume.go`) mapped each `convo.Message` 1:1 to one `transcriptEntry`, using only `Message.Text()`. The **live** rendering path (`finishAgentTurn`, `internal/tui/agentturn.go`) does something structurally different: a tools-enabled turn can append several `convo.Message`s to history (an assistant message carrying only `BlockToolCall`s with no text, a `RoleTool` result, possibly another such pair, then a final assistant message with the actual answer), and `finishAgentTurn` collapses that *entire turn* into **one** transcript bubble, prefixing the final answer with `toolActivityLines`' own human-readable summary ("• write_file hola.txt", etc.). `historyToTranscript`'s old 1:1 mapping had no equivalent grouping: an assistant message whose only content was a tool call rendered as a bubble with an empty body — just the header line — silently discarding the one visible record of what the turn actually did. This read to the user as messages having failed to load, when in fact they were present in memory but invisible on screen. **Fix:** `historyToTranscript` now walks `history` turn-by-turn instead of message-by-message: each `RoleUser` message still produces its own row, but a `RoleAssistant` message now opens a run that swallows every following non-`RoleUser` message (further assistant iterations, tool results) up to the next `RoleUser` message or the end of history — mirroring `finishAgentTurn`'s own `agentTurnState.before`-to-end span. The run's *last* assistant message supplies the model name and the final answer text (and the `[cancelado]` suffix, unchanged); `toolActivityLines` (already-existing, reused as-is) is called on a synthetic `&convo.Conversation{Messages: history[start:i]}` covering just that run, and its summary — when non-empty — is prepended to the answer the same way `finishAgentTurn` prepends it live. `missionRules` is passed as `nil` for a resumed run: there is no live `*permissions.Guard` to query on reopen (`Options` carries `RestoredMissions` for §21.16's own notice, not a `Guard`), so the one piece the reconstruction cannot recover is a dispatch call's inherited-constraint sub-line — every other line (tool name, target, pass/fail) still can, from the same block data that already survives on disk. `historyToTranscript`'s signature gained a `g glyphs` parameter (needed for `toolActivityLines`'s own first argument); both of its call sites (`NewRoot`, for `--resume`/`resume_last`, and `applySessionChosen`, for the in-session `/resume` menu — the only two callers, confirmed by `grep`) were updated to pass `lay.glyphs()`/`m.lay.glyphs()` respectively, so both paths benefit from one fix. **New tests**, `internal/tui/resume_internal_test.go`: `TestHistoryToTranscriptGroupsToolTurnIntoOneEntry` (a user message plus a tool-call-then-result-then-answer turn collapses to exactly 2 entries, the second carrying both the tool summary and the final answer), `TestHistoryToTranscriptToolOnlyTurnStillShowsSummary` (a turn with a tool call and result but *no* trailing text-only assistant message — e.g. captured mid-turn — still shows a non-empty summary instead of reverting to the old blank-bubble bug), `TestHistoryToTranscriptMultiTurnConversation` (two separate turns, one tool-using and one plain, sandwiched around two user messages, stay correctly separated into 4 entries rather than merging into one run) — plus the two pre-existing tests (`TestHistoryToTranscriptMarksAbortedTurns`, `TestHistoryToTranscriptSkipsUnknownRoles`) updated only for the new `glyphs` parameter, no behavior change to what they pin. **Verification:** sandbox had reset again since the previous session (Go toolchain missing, local git back on bare `main` with no `genspark_ai_developer` branch) — Go reinstalled (`go1.26.5`, matching `go.mod`); confirmed `origin/genspark_ai_developer` was fully subsumed by `main` (empty `git diff`) after PR #174 merged, so a fresh branch was cut from `origin/main` rather than recovered. `gofmt -l .` clean; `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green across all 26 packages (one `[no test files]`); `go test -race ./internal/tui/...` green. | 2026-08-18 | UX bug report · resize/window-move duplicates the visible chat — root-caused to an upstream `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` renderer bug, fixed by a dependency bump — **closed** | Third of the batch of UX issues from the "model pasted a whole file" report (2026-08-18 entry below): resizing or moving the terminal window during a session made past chat appear to duplicate on screen. **Investigation ruled out `internal/tui` first.** `Root`'s own `WindowSizeMsg` handling (`updateDispatch`, `root.go`) only rebuilds `m.lay` via `NewLayout` and reapplies the input prefix/width — no transcript mutation happens there. The pre-existing `evictOverflow`/`keepInline = 2` eviction mechanism (`root.go`, closed 2026-08-01 for an unrelated cursor-drift bug) was re-verified with a scratch reproduction test (written, run, then discarded — not part of the repo) covering a shrink-then-grow resize sequence: `printedUpTo` advances correctly on shrink and does nothing incorrect on grow-back. This confirmed the bug is not in `internal/tui`'s own model/update logic, but somewhere beneath `Root.View()`, in the bubbletea library itself. **Root cause, found by reading the vendored dependency source directly:** `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`'s inline-mode renderer (`cursed_renderer.go`) has a `flush()` optimization that skips redrawing entirely when the current frame's content and dimensions are byte-identical to the last frame's ("no changes, nothing to do"). `resize()` calls `s.scr.Erase()` to schedule a screen erase, but that erase is only actually drained the next time `flush()` does real work — if the very next frame after a resize happens to render identical content (common, since many resizes do not otherwise change the transcript or the live turn), `flush()`'s early return fires, the scheduled erase is silently skipped, and the previous frame's pixels are left behind underneath the new one, reading as "duplicated" chat. This is a generic bug in bubbletea's inline-mode renderer, not specific to ishakat's own rendering, and unrelated to the already-closed "no reflow on width change" decision (§7.5, confirmed 2026-08-03) or to the Termux-specific scroll-snap issue (2026-08-01) — both describe different, already-accepted or already-fixed behavior. Also found and ruled out as inapplicable: upstream issue #1567, whose suggested fix (`AltScreen = true`) contradicts ishakat's deliberate inline-only design; and upstream PR #1696, an earlier, unmerged attempt at a related but not identical fix. **The actual fix**, upstream commit `faf4dcf54a92bab2fe3bf6f4715adf44f2fc245d` ("fix: pendingErase in cursedRenderer", PR #1755, closing ticket CRUSHGH-1118), adds a `pendingErase bool` field to `cursedRenderer`, set `true` by both `resize()` and `clearScreen()`, and checked by `flush()`'s early-return condition so a pending erase can never be skipped — merged into `charmbracelet/bubbletea`'s `main` branch the same day as this investigation, but not yet included in any tagged `v2.x.x` release (`v2.0.8` remains the latest tag; confirmed by direct source inspection that it lacks the `pendingErase` field entirely). **Remediation:** since `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` is a vanity import redirecting to `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` (confirmed via `curl https://charm.land/bubbletea/v2?go-get=1`), Go modules' pseudo-version mechanism lets `go.mod` pin directly to the fix commit without waiting for an official tag: `go get charm.land/bubbletea/v2@faf4dcf54a92bab2fe3bf6f4715adf44f2fc245d` resolved to `v2.0.9-0.20260818073234-faf4dcf54a92`, and the downloaded source was confirmed (by grepping for `pendingErase`) to actually contain the fix. **This is a dependency-only change — no `internal/tui` source was modified.** No new test was written to directly exercise the renderer-layer bug itself: it lives beneath `Root.View()`, inside a private, unexported renderer type of a third-party module, with no seam ishakat's own test harness can drive (the existing `newHeadlessRoot`/`playTurn` helpers exercise `Model.Update`/`Model.View` directly and never construct a real `tea.Program`, so they cannot observe what actually reaches a terminal). This gap is accepted the same way this file already accepts the Termux scroll-snap limitation (2026-08-01 entry) — diagnosed with a named upstream commit and reproducible mechanism, fixed at the dependency layer, verified by full existing-suite regression rather than a new bug-specific assertion. **Verification:** Go toolchain (`go1.26.5`) present at session start this time — no reinstall needed; `gofmt -l .` clean; `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean after the bump; `go test ./...` green across all 26 packages (one `[no test files]`); `go test -race ./internal/tui/...` green — confirming the bump changes nothing observable about ishakat's own behavior while carrying the upstream fix. Files: `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `docs/PLAN.md`. |
| 2026-08-18 | UX bug report · code-block folding — rendering implemented, `ctrl+r` now actually folds/unfolds — **closed** | Closes the entry immediately below ("keybinding decided and wired, rendering not yet implemented"), the second of the batch of UX issues from the "model pasted a whole file" report. **Design decision:** a single `Root.foldCode bool`, not the per-block `map[string]bool` that entry's own "still missing" section had sketched as the leading design — `Root`'s Bubble Tea value-copy semantics (the same constraint `liveTurn`'s own doc comment documents for a different field) make a stable per-block key across re-renders awkward to thread through `finishTurn`/`commitEntryCmd` correctly, and a global toggle already fully answers the reported complaint ("the terminal gets too dirty") without that complexity — folding is "collapse what's currently filling the screen", not "remember which of forty past blocks I folded". **`internal/tui/codeblock.go`:** `renderMessageBody`/`renderCodeBlock` both gained a trailing `folded bool` parameter; new `foldSummary(g, lang, code)` renders the one-line `"▸ lang, N lines"` (or `"▸ N lines"` with no language) form, singular/plural handled correctly, dim-styled, still behind the same rail every other code line draws — folding is a content decision, not a layout one, so §9.3's rail stays. **`internal/tui/chat.go`:** `renderTranscriptLine`/`renderLiveTurn`/`commitEntryCmd` all thread the same `folded bool` through to `renderMessageBody`. **`internal/tui/root.go`:** new `Root.foldCode` field; a new `case m.keys.ToggleFold` in `handleGlobalKey` flips it and returns no command — deliberately *not* gated to `ModeChat` the way `ModelPicker`/`ThemePicker`/`CopyLast` are, since folding is a read-only view toggle over whatever is already on screen rather than an action that starts something new, so it stays reachable while `ModeBusy` is still streaming a long block (arguably the moment it is most wanted); `evictOverflow`'s `commitEntryCmd` call now passes `m.foldCode`. **`internal/tui/view.go`:** both `head()` call sites (finished transcript entries and the live turn) now pass `m.foldCode` through. **The one limitation inherited from §7.5, stated explicitly rather than left for a user to discover:** a transcript entry already committed to real terminal scrollback via `commitEntryCmd`/`tea.Println` (`evictOverflow`, `keepInline = 2`) can never be redrawn — inline-mode's own "never alt-screen" design — so `ctrl+r` only ever affects the still-live transcript entries plus the in-progress live turn, never anything already scrolled into real history; pressing it after a long session has scrolled a code block away does nothing to that block, by design, not by omission. **New tests:** `internal/tui/codeblock_internal_test.go` gained `TestFoldSummaryPluralisesLineCount` (singular/plural, with/without language, isolated from the rail/styling machinery per the same rationale `TestRenderCodeBlockDrawsTheRail` already states), `TestRenderCodeBlockFoldedCollapsesToOneLine` (rail survives, code content does not leak, fold glyph and language both appear), `TestRenderMessageBodyFoldedAppliesToEveryCodeSegment` (two fenced blocks in one message both collapse, prose segments between them are untouched). New `internal/tui/foldcmd_internal_test.go`: `TestToggleFoldKeyFlipsRootFoldCode` (mirrors `TestCopyLastAnswerSetsTheClipboard`'s own shape — first `ctrl+r` sets `foldCode` true, second flips it back, no command returned since this is a pure view toggle), `TestToggleFoldWorksWhileBusy` (pins the deliberate non-gating to `ModeChat` described above), `TestPlayTurnWithFoldedCodeShowsSummaryNotBody` (the real end-to-end check via `playTurn`/`m.View()`: with folding on before the turn streams, the finished frame shows the summary glyph and never the code body; toggling back off restores the full body). **Five pre-existing test call sites fixed** as a mechanical consequence of the new trailing parameter (`internal/tui/codeblock_internal_test.go` lines ~213/~233, `internal/tui/markdown_internal_test.go` lines ~69/~74/~92) — all `renderMessageBody` calls unrelated to folding now pass `false` for it, no behaviour change to what they were already pinning. **Verification:** Go toolchain was absent at this session's start (the same recurring sandbox-reset pattern nearly every recent entry documents) and was reinstalled (`go1.26.5`, matching `go.mod` exactly); `gofmt -l .` clean; `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` green across all 26 packages (one `[no test files]`); `go test -race ./internal/tui/...` green. | 2026-08-01 | Interlude · first hands-on session with the built binary | Six problems found by using the interface on a real Termux and a real PowerShell, all fixed before starting Step 8, because five of them are properties of the step-3 skeleton that Step 8 would have built on top of. **(1) Crash while streaming** — `panic: strings: illegal use of non-zero Builder copied by value`, reproducible by typing long text repeatedly. Bubble Tea v2 models are values: every `Update` copies the struct, and a `strings.Builder` held as a field records the address it was first written at, so the copy panics on the next write. `liveTurn.text` is a plain `string` now — anything stored in a Bubble Tea model must be safe to copy, and concatenation being O(n²) in theory is irrelevant for a turn of a few kilobytes next to a crash that takes the process down — and `internal/tui/chat_internal_test.go` plays a full streamed turn through many `Update` copies so a copy-hostile field cannot come back. **(2) Colour detection wrong on Windows** — the hand-rolled `theme.Detect` returned \"no colour\" whenever `TERM` was empty, which is the normal state of `powershell.exe` and `cmd.exe`, so every style was built flat: the banner was white there and a gradient in Termux, from the same binary. Detection is delegated to `charmbracelet/colorprofile` (the library Bubble Tea itself uses to decide what it may write, so the two can no longer disagree) plus a console-hint table for `WT_SESSION`/`ConEmuANSI`/`TERM_PROGRAM`/`ANSICON`. **(3) The logo was illegible** — it was six quadrant blocks (`▖▘▝▗`) arranged into shapes that spelled nothing, and those code points are absent from Consolas, so on a Windows console it was a grid of boxes. Replaced by a three-row pixel face that spells ISHAKAT using only `▀ ▄ █` — in WGL4, in cp437, and in every monospace font Windows has ever shipped. **(4) The repertoire was never a decision** — decorative characters were literals sprinkled through six render functions, which is why each earlier fix only moved the boxes elsewhere on screen. Added `theme.GlyphSet` (a second axis of terminal capability, orthogonal to colour, with `[ui] glyphs = auto\\|unicode\\|ascii`), one table per repertoire in `internal/tui/glyphs.go`, and an end-to-end test that plays a whole turn and fails if a single byte above U+007F reaches the screen in ASCII mode. **(5) Cursor and path display** — the terminal cursor was reported near the banner instead of inside the input box (`tea.View.Cursor` was built from the wrong origin), and the working directory printed as `~/ishakat` for `~/projects/ishakat` on Termux and `~/D:\\projects\\ishakat` on Windows: the display form was hand-built by string-replacing `$HOME` with `~`, which does not survive a drive letter or a nested path. Now `xdg.Pretty` (cross-platform, drive-letter aware) plus `tui.ShortenPath` (width-aware, abbreviates from the left). **(6) The binary would not run on Windows** — `make build` wrote `bin/ishakat` with no extension, which is not a program to the Windows loader, so PowerShell consulted its file associations and opened it in an editor; worse, a Linux ELF named `ishakat` had been committed to `bin/` in Step 1, so cloning on Windows was enough to hit it. The Makefile appends `.exe` on a Windows host, `make windows`/`windows-arm64` cross-compile with the suffix, and `bin/` is ignored. Finally, `ishakat doctor` gained the terminal section that makes all of the above diagnosable from a user's report instead of by guesswork: `theme.Diagnose` prints both decisions **with the variable that decided each**, the signals it read, and `tui.GlyphSample` — the logo and every decorative character, drawn from the interface's own table, so boxes, mojibake and \"the guess was right\" are told apart by eye. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `gofmt -l` all green. Not covered here and still owed from Step 3's closing criteria: manual verification at 40/60/120 columns and idle-CPU measurement, both of which need a real TTY. |

| 2026-08-01 | Bug report · input box cursor drifts off screen in a long session | Same user, third report, and the one this project already owed itself: the "debt for Step 8" entry above had measured a 64-row frame after 10 short turns at 24 rows but left the fix for Step 8's engine work, on the theory that nobody would hit it before then.
